questions.question:
Consider the given statement and decide which of the following assumption(s) is implicit.

**Statement:**

“You are expected to be honest before the advocate” — an instruction to be followed in front of a defence lawyer.

**Assumptions:**

1. Unless cautioned, the clients tend to hide certain vital facts to save themselves.

2. At times, the vital facts are required to strategize the defence argument.

‘Q + R’ means ‘Q is the husband of R’,

‘Q – R’ means ‘Q is the father of R’,

‘Q * R’ means ‘Q is the mother of R’, and

‘Q @ R’ means ‘Q is the daughter of R’.

If M + V @ P – U, how is M related to U?

Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.

5 * 25 * 5 * 11 * 9 = 23
In a certain code language, ‘EYES’ is written as ‘64’ and ‘NOSE’ is written as ‘65’. How will ‘LIPS’ be written in that language?

Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number.

76 : 16 :: 56 : 12 :: 21 : ?

Based on figures A and C, select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in figure B.

14 and 21

21 ÷ 14 × 3 + 48 - 37

HONK ∶ MPRK ∶∶ STAR ∶ TCWV ∶∶ LONE ∶ ?
In a certain code language, ‘FLEET’ is written as ‘TFMFF’, ‘OUTLET’ is written as ‘TOVUMF’, how will ‘LABOUR’ be written as in that language?

M B 6 & N C ! V 2 $ T 8 % 5 # 9 R S 4 @ 7 P

How many numbers are there which are immediately preceded by a letter and immediately followed by a symbol?

In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements.

**Statements:**

All fields are gardens.

All gardens are parks.

Some gardens are apartments.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some apartments are parks.

II. All fields are parks.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.question: Five boxes, A, B, C, D and E are kept in a vertical arrangement. Only one box is kept below box C. There are two boxes kept between boxes D and C. Box E is kept at the second place from the top. Only two boxes are kept above box A. Which box is kept at the bottom?

Decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the information given in the statement.

**Statements:**

During the rainy season many train accidents occur in hilly regions due to landslides.

**Conclusions:**

 
• Trains should not run during the rainy season.
 
• More precautions should be taken by the government to avoid landslides.
Find the odd one out from the given alternatives

Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series?

CTUJ, EVWL, ?, IZAP, KBCR

Eight children, C, P, D, R, E, T, U and F, are sitting around a square table facing the center of the table. Four of them sit at the corners, while four sit exactly in the middle of the sides. U sits immediate right of P. P and E are sitting diagonally opposite each other. R and C are sitting diagonally opposite each other. F sits immediate right of C. P sits second to the left of C. T sits exactly between R and P. Who is the child sitting immediate left of E?

Six friends, Govardan, Sarayu, Rekha, Shyamala, Hema and Ganesh, are standing in a queue at a ticket counter. There are two persons between Sarayu and Hema. Rekha is between Hema and Shyamala. Only one person is standing ahead of Govardan. Ganesh who is fourth from the back end of the row, is between Govardan and Hema. Which two persons are standing between Sarayu and Hema?

A question is given, followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements is sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and select the appropriate answer.

**Question: **Six people A, B, C, D, E, F are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Who is to the immediate right of F?

**Statement I: **E and C are immediate neighbour of B who sits opposite to A.

**Statement II:** F sits second to the left of B and third to the right of E.

options.text: Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not.
Either data in statement I or statement II is sufficient to answer the question.
Data in statements I and II together are sufficient to answer the question.
Data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not

D is an immediate neighbour of F to the right. Only one person sits to the right of B. E is not an immediate neighbour of G. How many people sit between E and A?
